harness: chapter/qa-p24-reentrancy.html (investigation only; qa-sweep14.html, qa-sweep-diag.html and all production files untouched)

added: per-render renderToken stamped on the iframe (f.__p24token) and re-checked before the gate, during every gate poll, and after the engine run
documentInFrame read back from the iframe location and compared with the requested chapter
overlapLog recording RUN-STARTED-WHILE-ACTIVE, iframe-busy-on-navigate, onload-for-foreign-token, render-token-stolen(-during-gate)
observe mode (records corruption) vs guard mode (rejects a stolen render instead of accepting it)

partTwo_control.mode: observe, one awaited run() at a time
partTwo_control.verdict: the instrumented driver reproduces the Phase 23 corpus state exactly — instrumentation does not perturb measurement
partTwo_control.incidentalFinding: 3 iframe-busy-on-navigate events fired in the clean run (a1-28, b2-50 ×2). All three are a retry navigating while the previous attempt of the SAME chapter was still marked busy — benign self-overlap inside the retry loop, not cross-run overlap, and none produced a wrong value.

partThree_overlap.configuration: two run() calls started 2ms apart, not awaited, same corpus subset, same iframe
partThree_overlap.subsetRationale: the P21 signature is chapter-level (a1-11 = 407/4/2). Two concurrent 259-chapter runs serialise into ~500 renders with 90s stalls per starved measurement and would not have completed; the anomaly neighbourhoods plus their immediate predecessors and successors test the same claim directly. A full overlapped corpus sweep was NOT run — stated as a limit, not a result.
partThree_overlap.observedFailureMode: STARVATION, not corruption. The later-starting run owns the iframe and completes normally; the earlier run's onload handler is replaced, so each of its measurements hangs to its 90s timeout and is then retried.
partThree_overlap.values: every record produced under overlap was correct: a1-11 412/3/1, a1-21 707/17/1, b2-07 655/0/0, b2-68 463/5/0, plus correct values for all six neighbour chapters
partThree_overlap.note: the driver page reloaded during the first overlap attempt (external), so only the winning run's records survived it; the test was repeated in tighter configurations below with the same outcome

partFive_b2_68.isolatedClean: 463 occurrences / 5 findings — matches the Phase 14 isolated re-measurement
partFive_b2_68.overlapped: two concurrent runs × 3 renders of b2-68 = 6 records, ALL 463 / 5. The starved run recovered on attempt 2 and produced correct values.
partFive_b2_68.verdict: the Phase 15 double-count was NOT reproduced by deliberate overlap in this driver structure

partSix_lifecycle.A_twoConcurrentRuns: tested — starvation of the earlier run, all values correct
partSix_lifecycle.B_runPlusReloadNavigation: observed accidentally during the first overlap attempt: the page reloaded mid-run and the in-flight run's records were simply absent from the store. No wrong values were written — records are lost, not corrupted.
partSix_lifecycle.C_storageKeyChange: NOT TESTED — deliberately skipped. The safe way to change the key mid-run is to navigate the driver, which is variant B; testing it standalone would have required deleting storage keys, which is off-limits.
partSix_lifecycle.D_persistExportDuringRun: tested — a 400KB localStorage write plus an 800KB Blob + createObjectURL fired 4s into a run. Values remained golden (a1-11 412/3/1, b2-07 655/0/0). No effect.
partSix_lifecycle.E_runRestartedBeforeCompletion: tested — second run() started 3s into the first, on the three anomaly chapters. All golden: 412/3/1, 707/17/1, 655/0/0.

partFour_p21Signature.observed: none of it. Across every overlap and lifecycle configuration, all three chapters returned their golden values with identical surface fingerprints. No occurrence undercount, no extra finding, no extra HCM.
partFour_p21Signature.classification: NO CORRELATION — overlap produces starvation and delay, never the P21 numeric signature

partSeven_driverSafety.detectsOverlap: YES — RUN-STARTED-WHILE-ACTIVE logged with both run tokens on every deliberate overlap
partSeven_driverSafety.silentlyAcceptsSecondRun: NO — the second run is recorded as startedWhileActive with its previousOwner
partSeven_driverSafety.recordsPageOwner: YES — activeRunToken plus a per-render token stamped on the iframe and re-verified at three points
partSeven_driverSafety.preventsCorruptResultBeingAcceptedAsStab: UNPROVEN IN PRACTICE. Guard mode ran under deliberate overlap and rejected nothing (rejected: 0) because the reject path requires a render token to be stolen mid-measurement, and that never happened — the loser never reaches the gate at all. The guard is correct but its rejection branch is untested against a real theft.
partSeven_driverSafety.changesMeasurementSemantics: NO — the 259-chapter control matched the expected values exactly

partEight_verdict.reasoning: Overlapping execution is detectable and does degrade the run (starvation, 90s stalls, retries, and — under an external reload — silently missing records), but in 4 lifecycle variants and ~40 overlapped measurements it never produced a wrong value. The P21 numeric signature was not reproduced once. Driver re-entrancy is therefore NOT established as the cause; the Phase 23 hypothesis E is not confirmed.
whatIsNowKnown: overlap causes lost/delayed records, not altered ones
a starved run recovers correct values via its retry loop
persist/export activity during a run has no measurable effect
a mid-run reload loses records rather than corrupting them
the Phase 15 b2-68 966-finding event remains unexplained and was not reproducible
partEight_verdict.p21AnomalyStatus: still unexplained after two dedicated phases. It is proven non-reproducible under clean single-run conditions (Phase 23, 2 sweeps) and under deliberately hostile overlap/lifecycle conditions (Phase 24). Treat the P21 sweep rows for a1-11 / a1-21 / b2-07 as discarded data, not as evidence of a mechanism.

authoritativeCorpusState.measuredBy: Phase 23 run1, Phase 23 run2, and Phase 24 control — three independent full sweeps, identical

nextExperiment: Stop chasing the P21 numbers. The remaining open item with real value is the Phase 15 b2-68 double-count (966 findings), the only observed event where a value was demonstrably wrong rather than missing. Test whether injecting qa-engine.js twice into ONE loaded document — which overlap can cause when both runs reach the same live page — produces duplicate findings; that is a single-page experiment needing no sweep. If it does not, close the whole line of inquiry: three independent sweeps agree, and the driver's real defect (starvation under overlap) is now characterised and cheap to guard.
